chunks: And al-Shaykh, may Allah support him, informed me from Abū al-Qāsim Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, from Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb, from a number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyād, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn Abī Naṣr, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Sinān, from Abī ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام, who said:

The deceased is shrouded in three [cloths], excluding the turban and the rag by which his hips are bound so that nothing of him may become exposed. The rag and the turban are indispensable, but they are not part of the shroud.

key_terms.الْخِرْقَةِ: the cloth used to bind the hips so that the body remains covered
key_terms.الْعِمَامَةِ: the turban placed on the deceased, treated separately from the three-piece kafan
key_terms.الْكَفَنِ: the burial shroud counted here as the core three garments
key_terms.الْمَيِّتُ: the deceased person whose burial preparations are being described
key_terms.ثَلَاثَةٍ: three cloths that make up the kafan proper

ai.seo_question: How many pieces are included in the kafan of the deceased in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling on the shrouding of the deceased. It states that the kafan consists of three pieces, while the turban and the cloth tied around the hips are necessary additions but are not counted as part of the three-piece shroud.
